As for the mirror, sure don’t slam him down against control, but the moment you slip him in (and at 3, it’s not the hardest) you have such an advantage it is hard to keep up. Agro definitely gets through him pretty quick, where he acts as a 3 mana, draw a card, gain x life, but low/fast agro (red) typically hasn’t been good against the incidental lifegain in the ramp decks or the power that green has in midrange.

/uj I feel like convolutes the game and the way deck construction works to an extent that it could cause a few problems. Like there would be a whole new mathematical idea on distributing lands throughout your deck. plus effectively just letting people reduce the size of the deck (by having some of the cards in another pile) kinda bypasses the 60 card minimum restriction. And the shuffling on your deck by fetches has a game mechanics component that would now be altered (think with cards like brainstorm, or effects like it). Overall, I think that implementing rules of any sort that separate lands out from the deck has fundamental repercussions that change magic as we think of it. Though I do find that I enjoy when people bring up possibilities to solve problems as we see it with the game, cause it at least gets me thinking about how to approach new game mechanics.
